# Satellite image registration: classic methods vs deep learning

> Measures how well classic and deep-learning methods recover the displacement between two Sentinel-2 images, to a fraction of a pixel, on accuracy and on compute cost. Displacements are simulated on real imagery, so the ground truth is exact. The code is the Python package `satreg`, under the MIT licence. The fine-tuned RAFT weights are published for research and for reproducing the results, and no commercial right is granted.

Methods compared: phase correlation (with and without a Hann window), SIFT, AROSICS, RAFT large and small (pretrained and fine-tuned on this data), LightGlue and RoMa.

Main result, the final evaluation on the 1,800 pairs of two held-out sites (a mountain and a desert): fine-tuned RAFT large is at 0.069 px of mean error and fails no pair, where pretrained RAFT large is at 0.095 px. Phase correlation with a Hann window stays more accurate on clean translations, 0.005 px against 0.030 px. The figures hold for 256 px windows of Sentinel-2 with simulated motion; none was measured on a pair someone supplies.

Run: `docker run --rm --network none ghcr.io/esamoun/ai-satellite-image-registration:1.0.0 register` lists the methods the container image runs. `satreg register REF MOVING --method NAME --out DIR` registers a pair of at most 512 px a side; there is no default method.
